THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.

 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FinitePresentationAlgebraMapFiniteStage
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionFace

/-!
# Reflection of the finite-stage triple-transition face equation

A descended triple transition and pair transition which agree with their transported
ambient maps satisfy the same compatibility with the two triple-model faces.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]

section

set_option linter.style.setOption false
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000
set_option maxHeartbeats 6400000

variable {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
variable (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
variable (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat)
variable (relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
variable (e : forall j,
  k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
    Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
variable (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
variable (mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
  Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
      (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
      (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
variable (hmapM : forall q,
  (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
      (AlgHom.id L.1
        (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
          (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
          (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
          (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
      ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
    ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
      L.1).comp
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
        (AlgHom.id L.1
          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))))))

set_option maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
-- Inference preserves the dependent ring instances already fixed by `mapM`.
/-- Scalar extension of the descended pair transition from `M` to `N`. -/
noncomputable def pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :=
  AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
    (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM (Sum.inr (U, V)))

include hmapM

set_option maxHeartbeats 6400000 in
-- Both component equivalences carry dependent quotient-algebra instances.
/-- Scalar extension of the descended pair transition to `k` is the transition
conjugated through the component model comparisons. -/
theorem pic0FiniteStagePairTransition_scalarExtension_eq_comparison
    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
        (R := M.1) (K := k) (mapM (Sum.inr (U, V))) =
      pic0FiniteStagePairModelComparisonTransition
        C L n m relation e M U V := by
  let EUV := pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv
    C L n m relation e M (Sum.inr (U, V))
  let EVU := pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv
    C L n m relation e M (Sum.inr (V, U))
  have hnat := pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv_naturality
    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM (Sum.inr (U, V))
  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
  intro x
  apply EUV.injective
  change
    EUV
        (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
          (R := M.1) (K := k) (mapM (Sum.inr (U, V))) x) =
      EUV (EUV.symm (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (U, V) (EVU x)))
  rw [EUV.apply_symm_apply]
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun hnat x

set_option maxHeartbeats 6400000 in
-- The pointwise form lets the inferred pair-map instances determine the source carrier.
/-- The finite-stage pair transition commutes with the canonical maps to `k`. -/
theorem pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange_ambient
    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    forall x,
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
        (AlgHom.id M.1
          (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
            (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C (Sum.inr (U, V))))))
          (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
            C L n m relation M mapM N U V x) =
        pic0FiniteStagePairModelComparisonTransition
          C L n m relation e M U V
          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
            (AlgHom.id M.1
              (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing
                C L n m relation M
                  (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C (Sum.inr (U, V)))))) x) := by
  intro x
  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
  | zero => simp
  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
  | tmul c a =>
      rw [AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul,
        Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul]
      rw [← pic0FiniteStagePairTransition_scalarExtension_eq_comparison
        C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM U V]
      simp [AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul]

variable [Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k]

set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
-- The reflected equation elaborates through three dependent tensor-product models.
/-- The ambient face equation reflects to a finite stage once the descended triple and
pair transitions commute with the canonical maps to the ambient field. -/
theorem pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModel_fac
    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
    (U V W : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C)
    (thetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
          C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
        N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
          C L n m relation M mapM p)
    (hthetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
          (AlgHom.id M.1
            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
              C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
          ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
        ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
          C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
            M.1).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
            (AlgHom.id M.1
              (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
                C L n m relation M mapM p)))) :
    (thetaN (U, (V, W))).comp
        (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
          (R := M.1) (K := N.1)
          (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceRight
            C L n m relation M mapM V W U)) =
      (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
        (R := M.1) (K := N.1)
        (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
          C L n m relation M mapM U V W)).comp
        (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
          C L n m relation M mapM N U V) := by
  apply DatG0.tensorProduct_algHom_comp_eq_of_baseChange N
    (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
      (R := M.1) (K := N.1)
      (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceRight
        C L n m relation M mapM V W U))
    (thetaN (U, (V, W)))
    ((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
      (R := M.1) (K := N.1)
      (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
        C L n m relation M mapM U V W)).comp
      (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
        C L n m relation M mapM N U V))
    (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
      (R := M.1) (K := k)
      (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceRight
        C L n m relation M mapM V W U))
    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
      C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM U V W)
    ((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
      (R := M.1) (K := k)
      (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
        C L n m relation M mapM U V W)).comp
      (pic0FiniteStagePairModelComparisonTransition
        C L n m relation e M U V))
  · have hval : N.1.val = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom M.1 N.1 k := by
      ext x
      rfl
    rw [hval]
    exact AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower
      (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceRight
        C L n m relation M mapM V W U)
  · exact hthetaN (U, (V, W))
  · apply DFunLike.ext _ _
    intro x
    have hval : N.1.val = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom M.1 N.1 k := by
      ext y
      rfl
    have hface := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower
      (F := M.1) (L := N.1) (K := k)
      (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
        C L n m relation M mapM U V W)
    rw [← hval] at hface
    calc
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
          (AlgHom.id M.1
            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
              C L n m relation M mapM (U, (V, W)))))
          (((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
            (R := M.1) (K := N.1)
            (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
              C L n m relation M mapM U V W)).comp
            (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
              C L n m relation M mapM N U V)) x) =
        (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
          (R := M.1) (K := k)
          (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
            C L n m relation M mapM U V W))
          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
            (AlgHom.id M.1
              (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing
                C L n m relation M
                  (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C (Sum.inr (U, V))))))
            (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
              C L n m relation M mapM N U V x)) :=
          DFunLike.congr_fun hface
            (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange
              C L n m relation M mapM N U V x)
      _ = (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
          (R := M.1) (K := k)
          (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
            C L n m relation M mapM U V W))
          ((pic0FiniteStagePairModelComparisonTransition
            C L n m relation e M U V)
            ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
              (AlgHom.id M.1
                (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing
                  C L n m relation M
                    (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C (Sum.inr (U, V)))))) x)) := by
            exact congrArg
              (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
                (R := M.1) (K := k)
                (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
                  C L n m relation M mapM U V W))
              (pic0FiniteStagePairTransitionBaseChange_ambient
                C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM N U V x)
      _ = (((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
          (R := M.1) (K := k)
          (pic0FiniteStageTripleModelFaceLeft
            C L n m relation M mapM U V W)).comp
        (pic0FiniteStagePairModelComparisonTransition
          C L n m relation e M U V)).restrictScalars M.1).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
            (AlgHom.id M.1
              (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing
                C L n m relation M
                  (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C (Sum.inr (U, V)))))) x := rfl
  · exact pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransition_fac
      C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM U V W

end

end


end AlgebraicGeometry

    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by

    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom

   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData

     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/

    65	/-- **CUSTOM.** The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with
    66	morphisms the morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/

    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]

    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]

   174	/-! ## Base change of fields
   175	
   176	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   177	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change

   179	
   180	/-- **CUSTOM.** Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e.
   181	`X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. -/
   182	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   183	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   184	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))

   186	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   187	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   188	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance

   199	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   200

   202	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
   203	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   204	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :

   211	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   212	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)

   215	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=

   226	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
   227	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId

   230	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   231	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
   232	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=

   235	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
   236	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   237	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
   238	    Over.pullbackComp _ _

   242	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor

   245	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   246	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   247	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]

   249	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
   250	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
   251	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
   252	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op

   255	canonical isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
   256	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   257	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   258	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   259	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
   260	  sorry

   262	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
   263	
   264	/-- **CUSTOM.** Identity coherence. -/
   265	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   266	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   267	    baseChangeIso k k C =
   268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
   269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
   270	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
   271	  sorry
   272	
   273	/-- **CUSTOM.** Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
   274	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   275	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
   276	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   277	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   278	    baseChangeIso k M C
   279	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
   280	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
   281	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
   282	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
   283	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   284	  sorry

   291	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]

    13	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
    14	
    15	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
    16	its structure as an abelian variety.
    17	
    18	## Status
    19	
    20	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
    21	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
    22	project from the witness directly.
    23	
    24	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
    25	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
    26	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
    27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
    28	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
    29	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
    30	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
    31	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
    32	
    33	`picardJacobianWitness` is wired to the `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development in its **étale** form
    34	(`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`): the witness scheme is `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C`, the identity
    35	component of the scheme representing the *étale-sheafified* relative Picard functor. It
    36	carries **no hypothesis on `C(k)`** — exactly the three challenge hypotheses and nothing
    37	else — which is the owner decision of 2026-07-28 (protection I-0491) and the full strength
    38	the challenge asks for.
    39	
    40	Why sheafifying is what makes that possible. Over an arbitrary field one cannot ask for
    41	representability of the *unsheafified* functor `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    42	(`picSharp`): Kleiman L5105–L5108 exhibits the conic `u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — a
    43	smooth plane conic, hence smooth, proper and geometrically integral, over a field where it
    44	has no rational point — for which he concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable while
    45	`Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is. The étale sheafification is Kleiman's own object; its sheaf property is
    46	*proved* in `Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`picEt_isSheaf_forget`), not assumed.
    47	
    48	**Two corrections to what this paragraph used to say** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30), both of
    49	which had already been made at the seam and in the blueprint and were missed *here*, in the
    50	file a reader opens first.
    51	
    52	*The reason was wrong.* This said `picSharp` "is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally". No
    53	source supports that for the **relative** functor: the lines it came from
    54	(Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302) are about the **absolute** `Pic_X`, and `picSharp` is *defined* by
    55	quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. Kleiman's own claim about the
    56	relative functor is the much weaker "not *a priori* a sheaf" (L1330), and `th:cmp` part 1
    57	points the other way — `Pic_{X/S}` *injects* into `Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever
    58	`O_S = f_*O_X` universally, automatic on these binders, so **in Kleiman** `picSharp` is
    59	Zariski-*separated* here.
    60	
    61	That last sentence is a statement about the SOURCE, and the Lean citation I first attached
    62	to it does not carry it (`review-ajc`, corrected in the same session by a fresh-context
    63	audit of my own fix). `PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`
    64	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) takes a `rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X`
    65	hypothesis: it says a *representable* `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf, by subcanonicity —
    66	which is the converse direction and is conditional on the thing the seam does not have.
    67	`PicEtSubcanonical`'s own §4 docstring scopes it correctly as "only the first half"; that
    68	caveat is what I dropped when I copied the citation here. Nothing in this project proves
    69	`th:cmp` part 1. Do not restore a Zariski-sheaf reason in this slot; two replacement
    70	citations have already been wrong in it (`I-0970`, `I-0973`), and this was a third.
    71	
    72	*And "**false**" overstates what is proved.* The non-representability of `picSharp` is a
    73	Lean theorem only *conditionally*:
    74	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
    75	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) derives from `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` that no scheme
    76	represents `picSharp C`. Its antecedent — that the comparison genuinely fails for that conic
    77	— is **quoted from Kleiman, not formalised here**; doing so means exhibiting `φ^*O(1)` in
    78	`picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image via `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`. So the accurate word for the
    79	unsheafified statement over arbitrary `k` is **unproved with a refutation route mapped
    80	out**, not "false". `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` says exactly this at
    81	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, and says that writing "FALSE" here is the error the board row
    82	was corrected for in the opposite direction.

    84	## The five obligations, and none of them is false
    85	
    86	Be precise about what the wiring buys, because "invoked upstream" is not "proved
    87	upstream". The witness reaches **five** open obligations:

    89	1. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` — representability of the étale-sheafified functor

   136	The two étale leaves are each stated at exactly the strength the assembly consumes, and

   189	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
   190	
   191	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
   192	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
   193	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,

   213	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
   214	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
   215	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
   216	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   217	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   218	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
   219	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
   220	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
   221	      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
   222	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g

   227	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   228	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
   229	  Classical.choose h

   232	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   233	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
   234	    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=

   238	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   239	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J)
   240	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
   241	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :

   245	/-- The Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the
   246	universal morphisms. -/
   247	theorem unique {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C}
   248	    {J₁ J₂ : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   249	    [GrpObj J₁] [IsProper J₁.hom] [Smooth J₁.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₁.hom]
   250	    [GrpObj J₂] [IsProper J₂.hom] [Smooth J₂.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₂.hom]
   251	    (h₁ : IsAlbanese C P J₁) (h₂ : IsAlbanese C P J₂) :
   252	    ∃! (e : J₁ ⟶ J₂), h₂.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ e := by
   253	  have ⟨g, hg_eq, hg_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
   254	  have ⟨h, hh_eq, hh_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
   255	  have ⟨g₁, hg₁_eq, hg₁_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
   256	  have g₁_eq_id : g₁ = 𝟙 J₁ := by
   257	    refine (hg₁_unique (𝟙 J₁) ?_).symm
   258	    simp
   259	  have ggh_eq_g₁ : g ≫ h = g₁ := by
   260	    refine hg₁_unique (g ≫ h) ?_
   261	    change h₁.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ (g ≫ h)
   262	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hg_eq, ← hh_eq]
   263	  have hgh : g ≫ h = 𝟙 J₁ := by rw [ggh_eq_g₁, g₁_eq_id]
   264	  have ⟨k₂, hk₂_eq, hk₂_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
   265	  have k₂_eq_id : k₂ = 𝟙 J₂ := by
   266	    refine (hk₂_unique (𝟙 J₂) ?_).symm
   267	    simp
   268	  have hhg_eq_k₂ : h ≫ g = k₂ := by
   269	    refine hk₂_unique (h ≫ g) ?_
   270	    change h₂.ofCurve = h₂.ofCurve ≫ (h ≫ g)
   271	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hh_eq, ← hg_eq]
   272	  have hhg : h ≫ g = 𝟙 J₂ := by rw [hhg_eq_k₂, k₂_eq_id]
   273	  exact ⟨g, hg_eq, fun g' hg' => hg_unique g' hg'⟩
   274

   277	/-- A bundled Albanese witness for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve
   278	`C`: a candidate group scheme `J` (with proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
   279	structure, smooth of relative dimension `genus C`), and a proof that `J` satisfies
   280	the Albanese universal property of Definition `IsAlbanese` for `C` *for every choice
   281	of $k$-rational marked point* `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`.
   282	
   283	Mathematically, the underlying scheme `J` (and its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
   284	structure) is intrinsic to `C`; only the universal morphism `C ⟶ J` depends on the
   285	choice of marked point `P`. Encoding `isAlbaneseFor` as a `∀ P, IsAlbanese …` field
   286	keeps the bundle independent of any specific pointing, which is what
   287	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve P` needs in order to project the Albanese morphism for
   288	an *arbitrary* input `P`.
   289	
   290	The smoothness witness is recorded at the specific relative dimension `genus C`,
   291	which is the form required by `Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`. -/
   292	structure JacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   293	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
   294	  /-- The candidate Albanese object. -/
   295	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
   296	  /-- The group-scheme structure on `J`. -/
   297	  grpObj : GrpObj J
   298	  /-- `J` is proper over `k`. -/
   299	  proper : IsProper J.hom
   300	  /-- `J` is smooth over `k`. -/
   301	  smooth : Smooth J.hom
   302	  /-- `J` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   303	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom
   304	  /-- `J` is smooth of relative dimension `genus C` (so dim `J = genus C`). -/
   305	  smoothGenus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) J.hom
   306	  /-- The Albanese universal-property data: for every choice of $k$-rational marked
   307	  point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`, the scheme `J` together with its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
   308	  structure satisfies the Albanese universal property for the pointed curve `(C, P)`. -/
   309	  isAlbaneseFor : ∀ (P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C), @IsAlbanese k _ C P J grpObj proper smooth geomIrred
   310

   173	    (htau : ∀ i, tau i i = AlgHom.id R (B i i)) (i : J) :
   174	    affineTransition B tau i i = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of (B i i))) := by
   175	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau i i).toRingHom) = _
   176	  rw [htau]
   177	  rw [show (AlgHom.id R (B i i)).toRingHom = RingHom.id (B i i) by rfl]
   178	  rw [CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
   179	
   180	/-- Construct `Scheme.GlueData` from affine ring charts, overlap maps, and algebraic
   181	transition coherences.  Openness and the diagonal isomorphism remain geometric assumptions;
   182	the transition identity, factorization, and cocycle are discharged from ring equations. -/
   183	def affineRingGlueData
   184	    (tau : ∀ i j, B j i →ₐ[R] B i j)
   185	    (theta : ∀ i j k,
   186	      AffineTripleTensor A B j k i →ₐ[R] AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)
   187	    (fId : ∀ i, IsIso (affineRestriction A B i i))
   188	    (fOpen : ∀ i j, IsOpenImmersion (affineRestriction A B i j))
   189	    (tauId : ∀ i, tau i i = AlgHom.id R (B i i))
   190	    (thetaFac : ∀ i j k,
   191	      (theta i j k).comp (affineTensorIncludeRight A B j k i) =
   192	        (affineTensorIncludeLeft A B i j k).comp (tau i j))
   193	    (thetaCocycle : ∀ i j k,
   194	      (theta i j k).comp ((theta j k i).comp (theta k i j)) =
   195	        AlgHom.id R (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)) :
   196	    Scheme.GlueData.{u} := by
   197	  letI (i j : J) : IsOpenImmersion (affineRestriction A B i j) := fOpen i j
   198	  exact
   199	    { J := J
   200	      U := fun i => Spec (CommRingCat.of (A i))
   201	      V := fun p => Spec (CommRingCat.of (B p.1 p.2))
   202	      f := affineRestriction A B
   203	      f_id := fId
   204	      f_open := fOpen
   205	      t := affineTransition B tau
   206	      t_id := affineTransition_self B tau tauId
   207	      t' := affineTripleTransition A B theta
   208	      t_fac := affineTripleTransition_fac A B tau theta thetaFac
   209	      cocycle := affineTripleTransition_cocycle A B theta thetaCocycle }
   210	
   211	end
   212	
   213	end AlgebraicJacobian
